text: Three seventeen. The bakery smelled like yeast and silence. Marisol slid the first batch of bread into the oven and noticed it again. In the wicker basket by the back door. The Borrowers, well worn. Every Thursday for six weeks, someone would leave it there instead of the library two blocks over. No name. No card. Just the book, smelling faintly of rain and woodsmoke. Tonight a folded note was tucked between pages 84 and 85. She wiped her floury hands and opened it. I can't make it to the library before closing. Please keep it another week. I like knowing it's warm. She looked at the basket, then at the tray of cinnamon rolls cooling on the rack. She chose the one with the most icing. Wrapped it in wax paper, tucked the note back into the book, and set both by the door. Then she flipped the sign to OPEN and started the coffee.
